ADB approves $ 200 m loan to boost MSMEs
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has approved a $ 200 million loan facility to help Sri Lanka strengthen micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs) by expanding access to inclusive finance, reducing credit information gaps, and building resilience to shocks.The financing package consists of a $ 100 million policy-based loan to improve the financial ecosystem for MSMEs and a $ 100 million financial intermediation loan to expand access to investment loans for MSMEs including $ 40 million for green loans.

Parliament panel calls for EV tax incentives, battery recycling rules
Parliament’s Committee on Ways and Means has called for tax concessions and policy incentives to promote electric vehicles (EVs), along with a proper system to manage used EV batteries, the Parliament Secretariat said. The Committee met last week, it discussed vehicle imports and the taxes on them, the promotion of EVs, and delays in clearing imported goods through Customs.

NCPI inflation climbs to 8.5% in Oct.
National inflation accelerated to 8.5% year-on-year (YoY) in October 2026 from 8.1% in September, as both food and non-food prices rose faster. The figures come from National Consumer Price Index (NCPI) data released by the Department of Census and Statistics (DCS) on Monday.
The reading ends a one-month pause in the climb. YoY inflation held at 8.1% in September after rising every month from 1.6% in February. A year earlier, in October 2025, it stood at 2.7%.

SL awaits final IMF board approval on 2 Dec
The International Monetary Fund (IMF) Executive Board has scheduled 2 December, to consider Sri Lanka’s 2026 Article IV Consultation and Seventh Review under its Extended Fund Facility (EFF) arrangement. The session will also cover requests for waivers of non-observance of performance criteria, modifications of performance criteria, and a financing assurances review. Executive Board approval will release approximately $ 345 million in fresh funding, bringing total disbursements under the four-year $ 3 billion facility to roughly $ 2.7 billion.

SL’s overseas missions generate Rs 6.6 b in revenue
Sri Lanka’s overseas diplomatic missions have generated Rs 6.6 billion (Rs 6,600 million) in revenue over the past period through services provided by Embassies and High Commissions, Foreign Affairs Minister Vijitha Herath said in Parliament. Herath further added: “As of the end of October 2026, $ 7.6 billion have already been received as remittances to the country. With an average monthly inflow of approximately $ 750 million, we can expect at least another $ 1.5 billion during the months of November and December. This would bring the total for this year to 9 billion dollars, surpassing last year’s figures and marking a new high for foreign remittances, which would be a historic achievement.”

Cabinet clears $30m OPEC Fund loan to support economic reforms
The Cabinet of Ministers has approved obtaining a $ 30 million policy-based loan from the OPEC Fund for International Development to support Sri Lanka’s ongoing economic stabilisation, recovery and structural reform program. The financing, offered following a positive assessment of the Government’s reform program and policy commitments, is intended to complement financial assistance provided by the World Bank under its Development Policy Operation. The proposed facility comprises $ 24 million from the OPEC Fund’s Ordinary Capital Resources and a further $ 6 million from its Special Capital Resources.

U.S.

stock futures were marginally lower on Tuesday night, following a slide in tech stocks during the regular session that drove the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite lower. Traders also looked ahead to fresh inflation data.

plunged 4.49% on Wednesday, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 1.41%. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200was down 0.41%.

Oil slumps to 3-month low on increased Middle East flows, Libyan pipeline restart
Oil prices fell more than 3% on Monday to settle at a three-month low on rising supplies from the Middle East and the restart of a Libyan oil pipeline, which offset worries about shipping and refinery attacks in the region.
Brent crude futures settled down $ 3.20, or 3.46%, at $89.37 a barrel. ‌US West Texas Intermediate futures settled down $3.24, or 3.88%, at $80.17 a barrel. Brent closed at its lowest point since 31 August, and WTI at its lowest since 10 August.Libya's Sharara oil pipeline has reopened, and crude is beginning to flow into storage tanks at the Akakus facility in Zawiya, the chairman of the National Oil Corp told Reuters on Monday.
